plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: A fragrant evergreen shrub with narrow gray-green leaves and dense spikes of small tubular flowers held on slender stems. It is widely cultivated in gardens and fields and is a favorite of bees and butterflies.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to late summer (June to August in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Mediterranean region, southern France, England, and cultivated worldwide in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: Lavender oil has been used since Roman times, and the plant's name likely comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash', because the Romans scented their baths with it.

plants.name: Rosa gallica
plants.description: One of the oldest cultivated roses, forming a low, suckering shrub with prickly stems and richly scented, semi-double flowers. Along with many other old garden roses, it peaks in mid-June in temperate gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (June in temperate Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Central and southern Europe, western Asia; cultivated in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Rosa gallica 'Officinalis', the Apothecary's Rose, was used medicinally in the Middle Ages and its petals keep their fragrance even when dried.

plants.name: Leucospermum cordifolium
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with leathery leaves and spectacular rounded flower heads packed with long, curved styles that resemble pins stuck in a cushion. It thrives in fynbos habitat and blooms as the Southern Hemisphere winter turns toward spring.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring (peak around August to November, with early blooms in winter months in the Southern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Western Cape, South Africa; cultivated in Australia, California, and Hawaii
plants.funFact: Pincushion proteas are pollinated by birds such as sunbirds, and their seeds are carried off and buried by ants, which protects them from fire.

plants.name: Lilium candidum
plants.description: A tall bulbous perennial with pure white, trumpet-shaped, intensely fragrant flowers on upright stems. It is among the earliest lilies to bloom in the northern summer garden.
plants.location: Eastern Mediterranean and Balkans; naturalized and cultivated across Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Depictions of this lily appear in Minoan frescoes about 3,500 years old, making it one of the oldest known cultivated flowers.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A large, graceful tree with fern-like foliage that is covered in clouds of lilac-blue trumpet-shaped flowers. In the Southern Hemisphere it is late autumn to early winter, but in warm Northern Hemisphere regions such as the southern United States, it is in full flower in June.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Northern Hemisphere (May to June); spring in the Southern Hemisphere (October to November)
plants.location: Native to South America (Argentina, Bolivia); planted in Florida, California, Texas, Mediterranean regions, Africa, and Australia
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, thousands of jacarandas create purple-covered streets, and a local superstition says that a blossom falling on your head brings good luck.
